title: Nested classes that use private members

blocks.text: The page's edge case: **a nested class can use the private members of the class that encloses it.** `Wallet` keeps its owner and balance in private fields and has a private constructor. Two nested classes work with those private members directly:

items: `Wallet.Builder` (a static nested class) collects `owner(String)` and `cents(long)`, and `build()` returns a new wallet made with the **private** constructor. Wallet must not gain a public constructor.
`Wallet.Auditor` (an inner class, one per wallet, from `wallet.auditor()`)
`report()` returns `"<owner>: <cents>"`, read from the wallet **at the moment it is called**;
`correct(long delta)` adds `delta` (which may be negative) to the wallet's private balance.

blocks.text: `deposit(long cents)` and `balance()` work on the wallet as usual.

cases.says: The builder makes a wallet, and its auditor reports the owner and the balance.
The auditor reads the wallet's private balance when asked, so it sees a later deposit.
A correction made through the auditor changes the wallet's own private balance.
Wallet has no public constructor: the only way to make one is its builder.

concepts: A class nested in another can use the enclosing class's private members.
